highlights.title: Kernel prepatch 7.3-rc4
highlights.summary: Linus Torvalds released the Linux 7.3‑rc4 kernel prepatch, noted for its large size.
highlights.detail: The prepatch continues the regular release‑candidate cycle for the upcoming 7.3 kernel. As usual, the diff is sizable, reflecting numerous new features and bug fixes accumulated since the previous candidate.

highlights.title: Pirate Face Rescues LLM Models from Deletion
highlights.summary: Pirate Face is a community‑shared method that prevents LLM models from being permanently deleted, as discussed on Hacker News.
highlights.detail: The thread highlights concerns about repositories removing older checkpoints and suggests using Pirate Face to archive copies locally, reducing the risk of losing valuable model versions. It emphasizes the importance of backup strategies for AI assets.

highlights.title: pandorafuture/wx-cli
highlights.summary: wx-cli is a Rust‑based command‑line tool that decrypts and queries WeChat databases on macOS.
highlights.detail: The utility handles the proprietary encryption used by WeChat, exposing chat histories and contacts for analysis or backup. Its open‑source nature allows users to audit and extend its functionality.

highlights.title: BuilderIO/agent-native
highlights.summary: agent-native is a framework designed to simplify development of agentic applications.
highlights.detail: The library provides abstractions for building autonomous agents, handling task orchestration, state management, and integration with external services, aiming to reduce boilerplate in AI‑driven software projects.

highlights.title: vercel-labs/json-render
highlights.summary: json-render is a Generative UI framework from Vercel Labs that creates user interfaces from JSON specifications.
highlights.detail: The framework translates JSON descriptions into UI components, simplifying rapid prototyping of web interfaces. It is hosted on GitHub and integrates with Vercel’s deployment workflow, targeting developers who prefer declarative UI definitions.

items.title: A Bandpass Filter Pulls In The Signals
items.summary: A bandpass filter can unintentionally admit strong nearby transmitter signals, causing front‑end overload even when tuned elsewhere.
items.detail: The article explains that proximity to high‑power transmitters can saturate a receiver’s front end despite the filter’s intended selectivity. Designers must consider isolation and shielding to avoid such overload scenarios.

items.title: Hackaday Links: September 20, 2026
items.summary: Sherline announced it will cease manufacturing operations after 52 years, planning closure by the end of October 2026.
items.detail: The company, known for its hobby‑machine tools, will wind down production and support. The announcement marks the end of a long‑standing presence in the DIY and small‑shop market.

items.title: Making a Copper-Oxide Photodetector from Scratch
items.summary: A DIY guide shows how to build a copper‑oxide (Cu₂O) photodetector from basic components.
items.detail: The tutorial walks through material preparation, electrode formation, and testing procedures, illustrating the photodetector’s response to visible light. It serves as an educational example of low‑cost optoelectronic fabrication.

items.title: Reverse Engineering A Sony Car Stereo LCD
items.summary: An Arduino‑based project reverse‑engineers the LCD of a Sony CDX‑A250 car stereo to enable custom control.
items.detail: The creator mapped the LCD’s communication protocol and built a driver that allows an Arduino to send commands, opening possibilities for aftermarket interfaces or diagnostic tools for the stereo unit.

items.title: Reviving TEMPEST Attacks with an Injected Signal
items.summary: A new technique revives TEMPEST attacks by injecting signals to capture unintended radio emissions from air‑gapped computers.
items.detail: By deliberately adding a signal, the attacker can amplify or modulate the emanations, making them easier to record and decode. This approach demonstrates that physical isolation alone may not guarantee security.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/train-llm-from-scratch
items.summary: train-llm-from-scratch is a Python repository offering a complete pipeline to train a language model from data acquisition to text generation.
items.detail: The project provides scripts for downloading public datasets, preprocessing text, configuring model architecture, running training loops, and performing inference. It is intended as an educational reference and works on typical consumer hardware with common deep‑learning libraries.

items.title: HelixDB/helix-db
items.summary: HelixDB is an OLTP graph database written in Rust that includes native vector and full‑text search on object storage.
items.detail: Designed for high‑throughput transactional workloads, HelixDB leverages Rust’s safety and performance while offering similarity search via vector indexes and keyword search via full‑text indexing, all stored directly on object storage backends.

items.title: Vita3K/Vita3K
items.summary: Vita3K is an experimental open‑source PlayStation Vita emulator implemented in C++.
items.detail: The emulator focuses on reproducing the Vita’s hardware behavior for research and hobbyist use, supporting a subset of games and system features while remaining under active development on GitHub.
